subject: Confusion with Regression output and plot

messages.subject: Confusion with Regression output and plot
parts:
Hi,

I am having some trouble interpreting the output with the semPaths plot of the same output. The specific relationship (among the many in the model) output is:

Mortgage:           estimate  Std.err  Z-value  P(>|z|)
 Income_O          0.000    0.000   68.727    0.000

However in the plot, this relationship is shown as the strongest relationship (i.e. thickest line) in the plot. Any idea what could be going on here? I assumed with the estimated coefficient of 0 it would not be shown as such.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: RE: Confusion with Regression output and plot
parts:
This could be a matter of scale differences between X and Y.  With a single predictor, a regression coefficient is essentially:

b = correlation(Y,X) * sd(Y)/sd(X)

If X has a very large variance and Y has a very small variance, then the ratio will be near zero, and so will b, regardless of the correlation.

 

If the result troubles you, take a look at the standardized estimate of the regression slope.

--Ed Rigdon
